correctness.rationale: Square completion gives the 1/sqrt(2) transform factor and the displayed Gaussian and phase factors. After scaling out the strictly positive intensity envelope, distinct pair sums give independent time exponentials. At each sum, the positive differences of its off-diagonal pairs are distinct (sum and difference determine the pair), and the constant if present and cosine/sine pairs are real-linearly independent. Their evaluation rows span the block dimension, so a maximal minor is nonzero for some frequency tuple, and its analytic zero set is null. Intersecting the finitely many generic sets proves the simultaneous rank formula; for every tuple below threshold a deficient block has a kernel. Exponential interpolation at any ordered distinct real times (by Rolle's theorem induction on the number of exponents) and extraction of m^2 independent rows prove the exact finite count. For m>=2 the Sidon criterion follows since any collision has weighted size at least three; the sine determinant is the criterion for the pair of lines jointly, not for individual lines. Second-line interpolation after subtracting the already known projections gives the stated optimal layout. The progression central sum has m ordered pairs; no sum can have more since each first index determines at most one second index. For m=1, one measurement suffices. Independently computed the stated exact 9-by-9 determinant by Vandermonde factorization and confirmed the progression ranks 8 and 9.
residual_risks: At or above threshold full rank requires a suitable frequency tuple; resonant tuples can fail. Exact linear Hermitian lifting only; no uniform stability or nonlinear minimality is proved.

evidence: Grohs–Liehr's geometry is (beta/2) Z times R, with continuous frequency. Wellershoff gives nonlinear uniqueness for bandlimited signals from two fixed frequencies and a time lattice. The indexed theorem confines its main result to finite integer frequencies and continuously observed periodic time profiles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Full-frequency reconstruction does not settle the sharp number of fixed-frequency scans. A nonzero finite Gaussian translate mixture is not bandlimited, and injectivity on rank-one vectors modulo phase alone cannot give injectivity on all Hermitian matrices.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Fourier transforming finite Gaussian translates yields Gaussian-enveloped tones, not periodic pure tones; interchanging the sampling axes also does not preserve the data geometry. originality.rationale: The strongest distinct indexed matches share a Gaussian multiplicity-block mechanism, but their periodic pure-tone measurements separate differences in time rather than sums in time and give a different rank and line count. The inspected Gaussian-shift reconstruction and two-frequency uniqueness theorems also differ in sampling geometry, signal class, or domain of injectivity. No inspected result covers the claimed exact fixed-frequency full-Hermitian rank and finite Sidon layout for arbitrary real translate supports.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a natural measurement-design question for known shifts and a fixed number of available frequency settings. Pair-sum collisions determine both the exact rank deficit and the optimal scan count; the difference between Sidon supports and progressions grows to m versus two lines. The precise resonance test and finite m^2-sample Sidon layout give information needed to design a successful exact measurement, beyond a qualitative uniqueness theorem.
residual_risks: Does not predict stability in noise or the minimum required by an algorithm restricted to rank-one signals.
